people.gloss: The silver candle by the painted screen, under the autumn stars (Đỗ Mục, Thu tịch)
people.role: Hall-mistress of Họa Tinh Đường since 1137, talismans painted with the Dipper in Mặc Yên soot
people.appearance: A slight, grey-haired woman in a black robe flecked with soot, who sits so still at the painting table that moths settle on her sleeves.
people.backstory: Kỷ Ngân Chúc was born in the dark-fungus village of Huyền Chi Thôn, the Hall's own, and is the founder Kỷ Thu Tịch's (ky_thu_tich) grand-niece. She ground ink for a thousand mornings before the founder let her hold a brush, and has painted the Pivot's Dipper talismans by the Silver Candle since 1100. The founder made the Hall in 910, sworn to the Pivot, and its talismans would not run in the rain (V059). That is why the Pivot's archive and its envoys use nothing else. When the founder died in 1137 she left the Hall to Kỷ Ngân Chúc with a key and an oath. The key opens a cedar box in the head's room. The oath is that the box is never opened while the Hall is the Pivot's. The box holds the founder's copy of Thorn and Ink Verses, a song art the Pivot has forbidden since it destroyed Cửu Thiều Cung (C005). The Hall's rain-fast ink comes from its blood-ink writ. She opened the box once, the night she took the oath, and has kept the oath since. The Hall's soot comes from the kilns of Mặc Yên in the vermilion pines, under her ink master Lăng Mặc Khanh (lang_mac_khanh).
people.wants: To stop the forged Dipper without opening the box, by some proof that does not say why the true one holds; and to keep painting until the candle burns down.
people.secret: The rain-fast ink every talisman of the Hall carries is a forbidden song art with the blood taken out, and every copy of the Compact the Pivot's archive has made since 910 is written in it. Sử Ngưng Mặc (su_ngung_mac) has known since the first ink the Hall sold her: she came north to the founder's burial in 1137 to tell Kỷ that she would go on buying it.

people.role: Chief painter of the Hall, holder of the Dipper Talisman Seal; selling the rain-fast stroke to Thính Vũ Lâu
people.appearance: A tall woman with ink to the elbow and a boxwood seal on a cord, who talks while she paints, which no one else dares.
people.backstory: A fungus-gatherer's daughter from the Hall's village like her master Kỷ Ngân Chúc (ky_ngan_chuc), named by her for the same poem. She holds the Dipper Talisman Seal and paints most of what the Pivot buys. She believes the rain-fast ink is the founder's honest discovery, and she has always wanted to sell it to every sect on the continent. This spring, in an inn at Khai Dương Thành, she sold the first half of its stroke to Hoàng Tiêu Diệp (hoang_tieu_diep) of the Tower's coast house, for more stones than the Hall earns in a year, and kept the stones.

people.wants: The second half of Hoàng Tiêu Diệp's price next spring, and her ink sold in every market south of the pines.
people.secret: She is selling the Hall's rain-fast stroke to Thính Vũ Lâu. She thinks the Tower wants the ink for its own writs. Its coast house wants the stroke to paint the Hall's Dipper without deer glue, so that the forgeries will hold in the rain and smell of nothing.

people.role: Ink master of the Mặc Yên soot kilns in the vermilion pines
people.appearance: A black-handed old charcoal burner with burnt eyebrows and a cabinet of a thousand ink sticks, each labelled with its year.
people.backstory: A charcoal burner's son from the dense pines of Mật Tùng Lâm, he keeps the Hall's soot kilns, the Mặc Yên, among the vermilion pines. They were built on the ash of the pitch town that burned in 712 (V055). He can tell the year an ink was made by its smell and the shine of a stroke. He keeps a stick from every year since 1100, and he has never been asked to use the gift on anything but forgeries. Kỷ Ngân Chúc (ky_ngan_chuc) is his master. He throws out whole firings for a smell he will not name, and the tappers who cut the wood for them go unpaid that season.

ties.note: the kiln girl
steward of the pine-tappers at the Mặc Yên kilns

tree.targets_note: Painters' route, then Creeping Vine and Strangler Vine from the Binding Vine idea: Wood debuffs, smoke and slow.

people.wants: To make one ink in his last twenty years that no one, himself included, can date by its smell.
people.secret: Each winter he burns one kiln on the ash of the old pitch town and bottles the soot as 'burnt-town ink' for a grave-seller in Khai Dương, so the Hall's pine count has run short since 1190. Diệp Tùng Yên (diep_tung_yen), who counts the pines, has begun asking where the wood goes.

people.role: The Hall's resident ink-maker at the Pivot's seat, who supplies the archive of the Compact
people.appearance: A neat, soft-spoken clerk in Pivot grey with the Hall's black cord at his wrist.
people.backstory: A scribe's son from Khai Dương Thành, he has lived at the Pivot's seat since 1160 and grinds the rain-fast ink for Tàng Ước Các. Its keeper Sử Ngưng Mặc (su_ngung_mac) trusts no other ink. In 1195 the copyist Thích Minh Thư (thich_minh_thu) asked him for a night's ink "for a guard roll of Tinh Tủy Mạch". He ground it and wrote the request in his book, with the date.

people.role: Keeper of the Hall's village and its fungus dyes
people.backstory: She grows the dark fungus that gives the Hall's paper its grey and its seal ink its violet, and runs Huyền Chi Thôn for Kỷ Ngân Chúc (ky_ngan_chuc). What the vats make beyond the Hall's need she sells at Khai Dương Thành's dye market. This year one buyer took ten jars of the seal's violet; she docked Thái Huyền Nhung's (thai_huyen_nhung) dye ration to cover the count.

ties.note: outer disciple from the deer meadow of Lộc Uyển
outer disciple at the fungus-dye vats of Huyền Chi Thôn

people.wants: A good price for the violet, and the granary of Huyền Chi Thôn full by the first snow.
people.secret: She knows ten jars of seal violet are not for cloth, and she sold them anyway, because the dye pays for the village's winter.
people.appearance: Wears her purse inside her sash, where no one in the village has ever seen it open; violet to the second knuckle.

people.role: Inner disciple of the head; sweeps the head's room and is taught by the Silver Candle
people.backstory: A dye-vat servant's daughter and Kỷ Ngân Chúc's (ky_ngan_chuc) last disciple, she sweeps the head's room, grinds the head's ink and is taught the rain-fast stroke by the Silver Candle itself. Tề Thu Ảnh (te_thu_anh) has not forgiven her for it. She leaves the head's ink pots uncovered for Tề Thu Ảnh to be blamed, and Tề Thu Ảnh scrubbed the head's floor for a month for it.

ties.note: inner disciple who paints the fourth star, Lạc Tố Bình's disciple

people.appearance: Sweeps with a stoop and smiles a beat after everyone else has stopped.

people.role: Inner disciple who paints the seventh star
people.backstory: Born at the Hall to two of its painters, he paints only the seventh star on the Pivot's talismans, the hardest, for Lạc Tố Bình (lac_to_binh), and has never spoiled one. He pays Hồ Mặc Nhi (ho_mac_nhi) a pine-nut cake a day to grind his ink for him.

people.appearance: Clean cuffs, in a hall where no one else has any.

people.role: Outer disciple at the soot kilns
people.backstory: A pine-tapper's girl of the vermilion pines who scrapes soot from the kiln roofs for Lăng Mặc Khanh (lang_mac_khanh) and is black from hair to heel by noon.

people.appearance: Sings off-key at the kiln mouths; her teeth are the only white thing on her by noon.

people.role: Outer disciple at the Pivot's seat, the ink-maker's apprentice
people.backstory: A Khai Dương boy who grinds ink for Hàn Thủy Mặc (han_thuy_mac) at the Pivot's archive and has made friends with every copyist in Tàng Ước Các. He trades what the archive's ink orders say for a cup of wine at the copyists' stalls, though Hàn Thủy Mặc has told him twice that the book is the Hall's, and found his own order list quoted back to him.

ties.note: outer disciple at the Pivot's seat, grinding the archive's ink

people.appearance: Laughs loud enough to be heard across the archive courtyard, and one ear is always inked.

people.role: Outer disciple from the deer meadow village; knew the forged Dipper by its glue
people.backstory: From Lộc Uyển, where the Pivot forbids hunting the deer (A086); she gathers fungus for Lục Thanh Chi (luc_thanh_chi) and will not paint with deer-glue ink. She knew the first forged Dipper by its smell: the glue is boiled in her uncle's yard at home. She sends him her stipend each season to stop, and he takes it and goes on boiling.

ties.note: outer disciple from the deer meadow of Lộc Uyển

people.wants: For her uncle to shut his glue yard before the deer warden finds it.
people.secret: The glue in the forged Dipper talismans is boiled in her uncle's yard at Lộc Uyển, and she has been paying him to stop.
people.appearance: Re-pins a twig of deer-grass in her hair every hour, dark-eyed and small.

people.gloss: An autumn evening (Đỗ Mục, Thu tịch)
people.cause: kiln soot in her lungs from three centuries of ink-making, at 317, at the painting table
people.role: Founder of Họa Tinh Đường (910); she painted the Dipper's stars and kept a forbidden book
people.backstory: A fungus-dyer's daughter who painted the Dipper as the Pivot's watchmen described it from Trích Tinh Phong (A084). In 910 she founded the Hall, sworn to the Pivot, and its talismans would not run in the rain (V059). She bought the book that made them so from a beggar in Khai Dương: a copy of Thorn and Ink Verses, carried out of Cửu Thiều Cung after its fall (C005). She left the Hall, the key and the oath to her grand-niece Kỷ Ngân Chúc (ky_ngan_chuc).

ties.note: her grand-niece and successor
